section_1.title: Introduction: Why Do Outbreaks Spread?
section_1.content: Briefly introduce the concept of infectious disease spread. Define the three key compartments: Susceptible (S), Infectious (I), and Recovered (R). Emphasize that individuals transition between these states.
section_1.example: Visualize a group of healthy students in a classroom where one person enters with a cold.

section_2.title: Defining the Compartments and Dynamics
section_2.content: Explain the mechanics: S to I (infection rate β) and I to R (recovery rate γ). Use a flow diagram with directional arrows to show the 'one-way' transition of population segments.
section_2.example: A 'health bar' animation: S (Green) turns into I (Red) upon contact, and I (Red) turns into R (Blue) after a set time.

section_3.title: The Core Equations: The Math of Flow
section_3.content: Introduce the differential equations (dS/dt, dI/dt, dR/dt). Use graphical representation: show how the slope of the 'I' curve is determined by the intersection of the new infection rate and the recovery rate.
section_3.example: A water tank analogy: Water flowing from Tank S to Tank I depends on the faucet width (β), and Tank I to Tank R depends on the drain width (γ).

section_4.title: Critical Thresholds: The R₀ Concept
section_4.content: Explain the Basic Reproduction Number (R₀). Define it as the ratio of β/γ. Explain that if R₀ > 1, the infection propagates; if R₀ < 1, it dies out.
section_4.example: An animation showing a virus spreading to 3 neighbors vs. 0.5 neighbors, illustrating the 'tipping point'.

section_5.title: Simulation & Application: Flattening the Curve
section_5.content: Demonstrate how changing parameters (like social distancing to reduce β) changes the shape of the 'I' curve on a graph. Summarize the model's predictive power for public health.
section_5.example: A simulation showing a 'spiky' graph (no intervention) vs. a 'flat' graph (simulating masks/quarantine), saving hospital capacity.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to keep left side for lecture
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
